name: Com tam
summary: Cơm tấm is broken rice with grilled pork, the Saigon plate kept when the broken grains were not sold. Pour sweet fish sauce over the hot rice: one plate is honey-glazed pork chops, a fried egg, spring onions, and pickled papaya; another is marinated ribs with an omelet, egg rolls, and sausages; a third is cucumber, pickles, pork skin, and pork patties under a candy-like fish sauce.
origin: Vietnam Tourism says farmers once kept the broken grains because they were not sold. The same bureau’s cuisine page calls the dish the essential Saigon plate, found on nearly every street.
history: Vietnam Tourism’s local-eating page says cơm tấm originated here: broken rice that farmers kept because the grains were not sold.
culture: One page calls it the go-to breakfast, and says people also eat it at any meal. The cuisine page says the smell of barbecued pork is on the street at all hours. The delicious-dishes page says breakfast, lunch, dinner, or supper.
texture: The cuisine page says the ribs are grilled over low heat so the meat stays juicy and tender. The photograph is rice, a chop, cucumber, and scallions. No egg is in that frame.
taste: The local-eating account says to pour a generous amount of sweet fish sauce over the plate. That sweetness is the sauce.
howToEat: The local-eating page’s plate is honey-glazed barbecued pork chops, a sunny-side-up egg, spring onions, and pickled papaya, with sweet fish sauce poured over the rice.

The cuisine page’s plate is marinated pork ribs on broken rice, with an omelet, egg rolls, and sausages, onion fat or pork grease, and fresh and pickled vegetables. The two plates are not the same list.

The delicious-dishes page’s plate is a little dry, small-grain rice, cucumber, pickles, grilled ribs, pork skin, and pork patties. It calls the fish sauce candy-like, and the soul of the dish: soak the hot rice in the sauce and eat it with the toppings. This plate is not the same list as the other two.
where: All over the center. Use the nearest room, and Cơm tấm Ba Ghiền at 84 Đặng Văn Ngữ, Phú Nhuận, is one clue. Grilled pork noodle bowls sit on afternoon sidewalks next to cơm tấm.
seoTitle: Cơm tấm in Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: Two sourced plates of cơm tấm in Ho Chi Minh City: the breakfast plate with sweet fish sauce, and the rib plate with omelet, egg rolls, and sausages.
